summary: Applies Python-style expressions to input CHOP sample values, recycling expressions across channels and preserving the first input's channel set and length.

key_params.name: chanperexpr
key_params.note: Channels processed by each expression before moving to the next expression

key_params.name: limitexpr
key_params.note: Limit the number of output channels

key_params.name: limitnum
key_params.note: Maximum output channels when limiting is enabled

key_params.name: expr0expr
key_params.note: Expression text; use me.inputVal or me.inputs[...] to access values

key_concepts: Modifies input channel samples using math expressions.
The output normally keeps the same channel names and sample length as the first input.
Each expression is applied to raw samples or keyframe values, then recycled when more channels exist than expression slots.
Channels per Expr controls how many channels use one expression before the next expression is selected.
Expression text can use me.inputVal for the current value and me.inputs[...] to read other input channels.
Evaluate DAT is the official companion when the goal is general expression evaluation instead of sample-wise CHOP processing.
common_gotchas: The output keeps the first input's channel names and sample length unless output limiting is enabled.
Expressions are recycled when there are more channels than expression slots.
Use me.inputVal for the current input sample and me.inputs[1][0] or me.inputs[1]['chan1'] for other input channels.
Per-sample Python expressions can be slow on large, high-rate CHOPs.
Use Evaluate DAT when the goal is general expression testing rather than sample-wise channel processing.
